source_refs.note: Book p. 88: Unit 6 INTRODUCTION (aims, number patterns (i)-(iv), explanation) and 6.1 Sequence (definition, terms, general term). Teaching notes, About this unit, Key points, Common mistakes are ours.

blocks.text: Assalam o alaikum bachon! Aaj se hum ek naya aur bohat dilchasp unit shuru kar rahe hain: Sequences and Series. Ghor karein to hamari zindagi patterns se bhari hui hai: har mahine tankhwah mein barabar izafa, bank mein paise ka har saal barhna, kisi bimari ka phailna, sarak par gaariyon ki ginti. In sab ke peeche ek rule hota hai, aur is unit mein hum yahi rules pakarna seekhenge.

Kitab is unit ke maqsad yun batati hai: hum arithmetic, geometric aur harmonic sequences aur series ke sawal samajhna aur hal karna seekhenge, aur dekhenge ke real life mein yeh kahan kaam aati hain. Hum mukhtalif qism ki sequences pehchanenge, finite (mehdood) aur infinite (la-mehdood) sums nikalenge, aur sigma notation (jama ka chhota nishan) istemal karenge. Phir practical misalein aayengi jaise motor vehicle leasing (gaari kiraye/qiston par lena), investment planning aur financial hisaab kitaab, aur healthcare, finance aur traffic modelling jaise shobon mein in ka istemal. Aakhir mein aap theoretical aur real life dono qism ke sawal sequences aur series se hal kar sakenge.
Chaliye shuru karte hain. Neeche numbers ke chaar patterns dekhiye aur har ek ka rule khud dhoondne ki koshish kijiye:

Pattern (i) mein har number (pehle number 5 ke ilawa) pichle number mein 6 jama karne se banta hai. Yani in numbers ki tarteeb mein ek pakka pattern chal raha hai. Isi tarah pattern (ii) mein har number pichle number ko 2 se multiply karne se milta hai. Pattern (iii) aur (iv) bhi apne apne fixed rule par chalte hain. Jab numbers ka koi set kisi pattern par chale aur agla number nikalne ka saaf rule maujood ho, to usay hum sequence kehte hain, jaise upar ki misalon mein.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Rule dhoondne ka aasan tareeqa: har term ko us se pehle wali term se milaiye. Pehle farq (difference) dekhiye, agar farq har jagah same na ho to ratio (taqseem) dekhiye.
(i) har baar 6 jama ho raha hai: \(5 + 6 = 11\), \(11 + 6 = 17\). Is liye agli term \(23 + 6 = 29\).
(ii) farq same nahin (6, 12, 24), lekin har baar 2 se multiply ho raha hai: \(6 \times 2 = 12\). Agli term \(48 \times 2 = 96\).
(iii) har baar 2 kam ho raha hai, yani \(-2\) jama ho raha hai. Agli term \(-4 - 2 = -6\).
(iv) har baar \(\frac{2}{3}\) se multiply: \(\frac{2}{3} \times \frac{2}{3} = \frac{4}{9}\). Agli term \(\frac{16}{81} \times \frac{2}{3} = \frac{32}{243}\).
Kyun yeh farq zaroori hai? Kyun ke (i) aur (iii) jama wale patterns hain, jinhein aage arithmetic progression kahenge, aur (ii) aur (iv) zarb (multiply) wale patterns hain, jinhein geometric progression kahenge. Poora unit inhi do khandanon ke gird ghoomta hai.

Ek rozmarra ki misaal se baat aur pakki karte hain. Kisi mahine ke saare Monday dekhiye: agar pehla Monday 3 tareekh ko hai to baqi 10, 17, 24 tareekh ko honge. Har baar 7 din jama ho rahe hain, kyun ke hafte mein 7 din hain. Yeh bhi ek sequence hai, aur iska rule hum pehle se jaante hain. Isi tarah agar kisi ke paas 1000 rupay hon aur woh har din 100 rupay kharch kare to baqi raqam 900, 800, 700... ek ghatti hui sequence banati hai. Yaad rakhiye: sequence ki pehchan uska rule hai, sirf numbers ki list nahin. Jab tak rule saaf na ho, hum agla number yaqeen se nahin bata sakte.

Ab definition. Kisi diye hue rule ke mutabiq numbers ki bataraiqa (systematic) tarteeb ko sequence (silsila) kehte hain. Sequence ke numbers ko us ki terms kehte hain. Pehli term ko hum \(a_{1}\) likhte hain, doosri ko \(a_{2}\), aur isi tarah aage. Sequence ki \(n\)th term ko \(a_{n}\) se zahir karte hain; isay general term (aam term) bhi kehte hain, kyun ke \(n\) ki jagah koi bhi position rakh kar woh term mil jati hai. \(a_{n}\) se foran pehle wali terms ko \((n-1)\)st term, \((n-2)\)nd term waghera kehte hain.

blocks.text_alt: a sub 1, a sub 2, a sub 3, and so on up to a sub n minus 1, a sub n, and so on

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
\(a_{n}\) ko "a sub n" parhte hain. Neeche likha chhota \(n\) sirf term ki jagah (position) batata hai: pehli, doosri, teesri... Yeh power nahin aur multiply bhi nahin. Is liye \(a_{3}\) ka matlab hai "teesri term", \(a \times 3\) nahin.
Misal ke taur par class mein bachon ke roll numbers socheiye: roll number 1 wala pehla, roll number 2 wala doosra. Roll number sirf jagah batata hai, bachay ki umar ya qad nahin. Bilkul isi tarah subscript sirf jagah batata hai.
General term ek formula hai jo position se term de deta hai. Pattern (i) ke liye \(a_{n} = 6n - 1\). Tasdeeq: \(a_{1} = 6 - 1 = 5\), \(a_{2} = 12 - 1 = 11\), \(a_{3} = 17\), \(a_{4} = 23\). Bilkul wahi numbers!
Kyun yeh formula itna kaam ka hai? Kyun ke 100th term chahiye ho to 99 terms likhne ki zaroorat nahin: seedha \(a_{100} = 600 - 1 = 599\).
Chunke \(n\) ki values \(1, 2, 3, \ldots\) hoti hain, is liye sequence asal mein ek rule (function) hai jis ka input natural numbers hain. Poori sequence ko aksar \(\{a_{n}\}\) likhte hain.
Agar \(n\) kisi term ki position hai to us se pichli term position \(n - 1\) par hai aur us se pichli \(n - 2\) par: \(a_{n-1}\), \(a_{n-2}\).

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
1. Pattern (iii) \(4, 2, 0, -2, \ldots\) ki \(a_{5}\) aur \(a_{6}\) kya hain? (Jawab: \(-4\) aur \(-6\).)
2. Agar \(n = 10\) ho to \(a_{n-1}\) kaun si term hai? (Jawab: 9th term, \(a_{9}\).)
3. Kya \(1, 7, 2, 9, 4\) sequence hai? Agar koi saaf rule nazar na aaye to kitab ki definition ke mutabiq yeh sequence nahin kehlayegi.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
(Yeh hamari apni misaal hai, kitab ki nahin.) Pattern (iii) ka general term dhoondte hain. Pehli term 4 hai aur har qadam par 2 kam hota hai. \(n\)th term tak pahunchne ke liye \(n - 1\) qadam lagte hain, is liye
\[a_{n} = 4 - 2(n-1)\]
\[a_{n} = 6 - 2n\]
Tasdeeq: \(a_{1} = 6 - 2 = 4\), \(a_{2} = 6 - 4 = 2\), \(a_{3} = 0\), \(a_{5} = 6 - 10 = -4\). Sab sahi!

blocks.title: About this unit
blocks.text:
Unit 6 ka raasta: 6.1 sequences, 6.2 aur 6.3 arithmetic progression aur arithmetic means, 6.4 series (jama), 6.5 se 6.7 geometric progression, geometric means aur geometric series, phir arithmetico-geometric aur harmonic progressions aur un ke istemal.
Pichli classon se yeh cheezein yaad honi chahiye: expression mein numbers rakhna (substitution), linear equations hal karna, aur fractions aur surds (jaise \(\sqrt{2}\)) ko simplify karna.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Sequence numbers ki aisi tarteeb hai jo ek pakke rule par chale.
2. Us ke numbers terms kehlate hain: \(a_{1}\) pehli term, \(a_{2}\) doosri, \(a_{n}\) \(n\)th ya general term.
3. \(a_{n}\) se pehle wali terms \(a_{n-1}\) (\((n-1)\)st) aur \(a_{n-2}\) (\((n-2)\)nd) hain.
4. Pattern ka rule dhoondne ke liye har term ko pichli term se milaiye: pehle farq, phir ratio.
5. General term mil jaye to koi bhi term seedha nikal sakte hain.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. \(a_{n}\) ko \(a \times n\) ya \(a^{n}\) samajhna: subscript sirf jagah batata hai.
2. Har numbers ki list ko sequence keh dena: agli term ka saaf rule hona zaroori hai.
3. \(a_{n-1}\) (pichli term) ki jagah \(a_{n} - 1\) likh dena: \(a_{n} - 1\) ka matlab hai "\(n\)th term mein se ek kam", jo bilkul alag cheez hai. Bachne ka tareeqa: \(n - 1\) ko hamesha subscript ke andar likhiye.
4. Rule sirf pehli do terms se tay kar lena: kam az kam teen chaar terms par rule check kijiye.
